status_detail: Three-pass production review published 31 exact, previously absent SHA-256 indicators from four direct research reports: 18 malicious stages from Huntress's active ClickFix-delivered custom RAT campaign (at least 40 incidents and two live variants), five Star Blizzard RedFlick delivery artifacts from Microsoft Threat Intelligence, two new Macfinger macOS stealer artifacts and three LausivLoader stages from SANS ISC, and three NeedyMantis loader/archive artifacts from Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The over-10 ClickFix family exception is justified by the campaign's scale, two current variants, and distinct executable stages recovered from affected hosts. Daily-Threat-Intel supplied five network indicators and no file hashes. Sixty-six recent MalwareBazaar browse candidates were rejected because individual metadata-rich sample records could not be accessed; browse labels alone were not accepted. The review also excluded two legitimate signed sideloading hosts explicitly marked do-not-block by Huntress, six CLOSEDQUORUM research builds without confirmed in-the-wild deployment, cumulative duplicates, non-file/certificate/configuration indicators, and current reports that did not publish exact SHA-256 values. Sixteen distinct sources were directly reached across primary research and security-news discovery; SecurityWeek returned HTTP 403. The Hacker News independently repeated the three exact NeedyMantis hashes but attributed them solely to Microsoft, so independent exact-hash corroboration remains zero.
